title: Rajya Vijay: Territory Conquest
description: Lead your forces across the battlefield! Capture territories, defeat enemy units, and claim victory through strategic positioning and smart resource management. Inspired by the great kingdoms of ancient India.
learning_objectives: Develop strategic planning and tactical decision-making skills
Practice spatial reasoning and positional awareness on a grid-based battlefield
Learn resource management through unit health, positioning, and turn economy
Understand cost-benefit trade-offs in offensive vs defensive strategies
Explore Indian historical kingdoms, forts, and military strategy concepts

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Command your army on an 8x10 grid battlefield -- your fort is at the bottom-left, the enemy fort is at the top-right
Each turn, select a unit, then choose to Move or Attack (each unit can do one action per turn)
Move units within their move_range to reposition -- cavalry moves fastest, siege engines move slowest
Attack enemy units within your attack_range -- melee units must be adjacent, ranged units can strike from afar
Capture cities by moving a unit onto an unoccupied city tile and holding it for one full turn
Defeat all enemy units OR capture all three cities to win before the 15-turn limit!
tips: Use your Archer and Cavalry to scout and control the map early -- they have superior range and speed
Protect your Siege Engine -- it deals massive damage but is slow and fragile
Forests provide a defense bonus, mountains block movement -- use terrain to your advantage
Capturing cities gives you score bonuses and denies the enemy strategic positions
Focus fire on one enemy unit at a time rather than spreading damage across many

plain.description: Open ground with no bonuses or penalties

forest.description: Dense trees provide cover -- units here gain +3 defense

mountain.description: High ground gives +5 defense but costs 2 movement to enter

water.description: Rivers and lakes block all ground movement

city.description: Fortified settlements grant +4 defense and can be captured for victory points

base.description: Your home fort -- heavily fortified starting position

enemy_base.description: The enemy's stronghold -- the ultimate target

units.name: Yoddha (Warrior)
units.description: A battle-hardened foot soldier of the Chola army. Strong in close combat with solid defense. The backbone of your forces.

units.name: Dhanurdhari (Archer)
units.description: A skilled bowman trained in the art of Dhanurveda. Strikes from a distance but crumbles in melee. Keep behind your warriors.

units.name: Ashvarohi (Cavalry)
units.description: A swift horseman of the royal cavalry. Covers vast ground in a single turn -- perfect for flanking, scouting, and capturing cities.

units.name: Yantra (Siege Engine)
units.description: A massive stone-throwing war machine. Devastating long-range firepower but extremely slow and fragile. Protect it at all costs.

enemy_units.name: Kalinga Sainik
enemy_units.description: A disciplined Kalinga foot soldier who charges toward the nearest threat.

enemy_units.name: Kalinga Dhanush
enemy_units.description: An enemy archer who maintains distance and picks off weakened units from safety.

enemy_units.name: Kalinga Ashvarohi
enemy_units.description: A fast enemy horseman who tries to circle around and attack your ranged or siege units.

enemy_units.name: Kalinga Rakshak
enemy_units.description: A heavily armoured guardian who protects the Kalinga Citadel. Hard to kill but slow.

enemy_units.name: Senapati (Commander)
enemy_units.description: The enemy general who commands with intelligence. Targets your most valuable units and retreats when outmatched.

objectives.description: Capture the ancient capital of Pataliputra

conditions.description: Failed to achieve objectives within 15 turns

glossary_terms.definition: A Sanskrit word meaning warrior or fighter. In ancient India, Yoddhas were trained soldiers who formed the backbone of any army.
glossary_terms.example: The Chola Yoddha unit is your melee fighter with high HP and strong close-combat attack.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Yoddha = Your frontline fighter who does the heavy hitting.

glossary_terms.definition: One who wields a bow (dhanush). The science of archery in ancient India was called Dhanurveda and was considered a sacred martial art.
glossary_terms.example: Your Dhanurdhari can attack enemies 3 tiles away without being in danger of melee counterattack.

glossary_terms.definition: A horse-mounted soldier. Ashva means horse in Sanskrit. Cavalry units were prized for their speed and ability to flank enemy formations.
glossary_terms.example: The Ashvarohi can move 4 tiles per turn, making it ideal for capturing distant cities.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Ashva = horse, so Ashvarohi = one who rides a horse.

glossary_terms.definition: The commander-in-chief of an army in ancient Indian kingdoms. The Senapati held one of the highest military positions in the royal court.
glossary_terms.example: The enemy Senapati unit has balanced stats and smart AI behavior, making it the most dangerous foe.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Sena = army, Pati = lord. Senapati = Lord of the Army.

glossary_terms.definition: Means 'Kingdom Victory' or 'Conquest of the Realm' in Sanskrit. It refers to the strategic expansion of a kingdom through military and diplomatic means.
glossary_terms.example: The game title Rajya Vijay represents your quest to conquer territories and expand your kingdom.
glossary_terms.remember_tip: Rajya = Kingdom, Vijay = Victory. Like winning a kingdom!

achievements.title: Samrat (Emperor)
achievements.description: Capture all 3 cities in a single game

achievements.title: Invincible Legion
achievements.description: Win without losing any of your 4 units
